strengths: Clear problem identification and elegant solution: Standard Conditional Flow Matching (CFM) applied to inverse problems requires concatenating latent noise and performance labels into a source vector that flows to design parameters, creating an artificial coordinate-coupling artifact sensitive to ordering. Diag-CFM resolves this by augmenting the state space to (P+L) and zero-anchoring labels ([z; y] -> [x; 0_L]), which provably restores coordinate permutation equivariance.

Compelling architecture-intrinsic uncertainty quantification: The zero-anchoring construction naturally yields 'Zero-Deviation' (checking whether the label components vanish at t=1) at zero marginal inference cost, as well as 'Self-Consistency' (resetting zero-channels and integrating backward). Both metrics consistently outperform computationally expensive deep ensembles and flow-matching loss baselines across multiple downstream tasks.

Rigorous and multi-faceted empirical validation: Evaluated across realistic engineering domains (turbomachinery combustor and transonic airfoil aerodynamics) and a scalable multi-objective analytical benchmark (DTLZ2 up to P=100). The paper rigorously assesses forward accuracy, round-trip inverse accuracy, candidate selection, error rejection, and out-of-distribution detection.

Insightful evaluation of generative diversity: The accuracy-conditioned diversity analysis convincingly demonstrates that raw diversity metrics are deceptive when baselines generate inaccurate designs, proving Diag-CFM genuinely maintains meaningful solution diversity among physically valid designs.
weaknesses: Contextualization with augmented ODEs: Zero-anchoring by augmenting the state space with extra zero-targeted coordinates shares conceptual similarities with Augmented Neural ODEs (ANODEs, Dupont et al., 2019). While the context here is flow matching for conditional inverse problems, discussing this connection would place the architectural choice in broader context.

Forward MSE degradation at higher dimensions: On the DTLZ2 benchmark at P=50 and P=100 (Table 3), the coupling-based INN baseline achieves lower forward MSE than Diag-CFM (even though Diag-CFM retains a massive advantage on inverse round-trip error). While the authors acknowledge this limitation, a deeper explanation for why forward surrogate modeling degrades in high dimensions would strengthen the paper.

Sensitivity to numerical ODE solver parameters: Both generation and the uncertainty metrics rely on explicit Euler integration with 30 steps. The manuscript lacks an ablation on solver tolerances or step sizes, particularly concerning whether Zero-Deviation is sensitive to numerical integration drift.

strengths: The paper identifies an important and overlooked failure mode when adapting bidirectional conditional flow matching (CFM) to inverse problems: the arbitrary pairing of design coordinates with labels causes severe sensitivity to coordinate ordering and scaling mismatch.

The proposed Diagonal Flow Matching (Diag-CFM) formulation is clean, simple, and elegant. By zero-anchoring labels and pairing all design coordinates with latent noise, the target velocity distribution becomes provably equivariant to coordinate permutations, completely eliminating ordering sensitivity.

The architecture-intrinsic uncertainty quantification metrics—Zero-Deviation and Self-Consistency—are clever byproducts of the zero-anchoring design. In particular, Zero-Deviation provides an effective measure of epistemic uncertainty at zero additional inference cost.

The experimental evaluation is rigorous and thorough across three distinct engineering and benchmark tasks (gas turbine combustor, Unifoil aerodynamics, and scalable DTLZ), demonstrating substantial improvements in round-trip error and convincing utility in candidate selection, abstention, and out-of-distribution detection.
weaknesses: The baseline choice for CFM is framed around an augmented state formulation [z; y] -> x (adopted from the invertible neural network literature). In standard conditional generative modeling (e.g., standard conditional diffusion/CFM), conditioning y is typically fed directly to the vector field network v(t, x, y) mapping z in R^P to x in R^P, with a separate forward surrogate. The paper would benefit from a more explicit discussion and empirical comparison with standard unidirectional conditional flow matching + surrogate baselines.
The theoretical contributions (Propositions 4.1 and 4.2) are somewhat elementary, largely formalizing the straightforward coordinate-wise decoupling of X and Y.

Using a P-dimensional latent noise z in R^P alongside L zero-anchored coordinates results in an augmented space R^{P+L}, whereas the underlying intrinsic manifold of design solutions is typically (P - L)-dimensional. The paper does not thoroughly analyze whether expanding to P latent noise dimensions introduces excess latent degrees of freedom or affects the regularity of the inverse mapping.

strengths: Clear identification of a practical pathology: The paper clearly identifies and formalizes a significant shortcoming in applying standard augmented Conditional Flow Matching (CFM) to inverse problems—specifically, the sensitivity of the learning objective to arbitrary coordinate ordering and scale mismatches when concatenating latents and conditioning labels.

Simple, elegant, and theoretically grounded formulation: The proposed Diagonal Flow Matching (Diag-CFM) zero-anchoring strategy ([z; y] -> [x; 0]) elegantly decouples design parameters and labels in the regression target, restoring coordinate permutation equivariance without requiring heuristic coordinate matching.

Zero-overhead architecture-specific uncertainty quantification: Deriving the 'Zero-Deviation' metric directly from the flow's endpoint provides a clever, effective epistemic uncertainty signal as a free byproduct of sampling, eliminating the computational burden of deep ensembles or repeated rollouts.

Strong and consistent empirical validation: Diag-CFM demonstrates order-of-magnitude improvements in round-trip reconstruction error across multiple benchmarks (gas turbine combustor, Unifoil aerodynamics, and DTLZ2 up to P=100) compared to standard CFM and coupling-based INNs, while maintaining meaningful design diversity under strict error thresholds.

Comprehensive evaluation of UQ capabilities: The paper rigorously tests uncertainty metrics across three distinct, practical engineering tasks—candidate selection (select-best), selective abstention (error-rejection), and out-of-distribution detection—where Zero-Deviation and Self-Consistency consistently outperform deep ensembles and flow matching loss baselines.
weaknesses: Missing comparison to standard conditional diffusion/flow baselines: The paper compares Diag-CFM against an augmented-space CFM baseline and coupling-based INNs. However, it lacks empirical comparisons against standard unidirectional conditional diffusion/CFM models that condition on y via concatenation/cross-attention (i.e., generating x from z conditioned on y without bidirectionality), which would help isolate the exact trade-off between bidirectionality and conditional generation quality.

Forward predictive degradation in high dimensions: As reported in Table 3 on the DTLZ2 benchmark, Diag-CFM's forward prediction MSE degrades significantly as dimension scales to P=50 and P=100, where coupling-based INNs achieve lower error. While acknowledged in the limitations, the paper does not offer an architectural or mechanistic explanation for this behavior.

High-dimensional testing is confined to synthetic benchmarks: Although the scalability is verified up to P=100 on the analytical DTLZ2 test suite, the physical engineering tasks remain low-dimensional (P=6 and P=14). Demonstrating performance on a higher-dimensional physical inverse problem (e.g., full shape parameterization or field inversion) would strengthen the practical impact.

Overstated theoretical novelty: Proposition 4.1 and 4.2 essentially state elementary properties of i.i.d. noise vectors under coordinate permutation matrices; framing these straightforward observations as major formal propositions somewhat overstates the mathematical contribution.

strengths: The proposed zero-anchoring strategy (Diag–CFM) is simple, elegant, and mathematically well-motivated: by setting the target velocity to [x - z; -y], it completely eliminates the sensitivity to coordinate ordering and dimensional scale mixing present in standard CFM for inverse problems.

The architecture-specific uncertainty quantification metric, Zero-Deviation, is particularly clever and practical: because the flow is trained to push the label coordinates to zero at t=1, the deviation from zero serves as an effective epistemic uncertainty signal that comes completely free as a byproduct of sampling (requiring zero additional forward passes or ensemble training).

The experimental evaluation is extensive, spanning five diverse domains: gas turbine combustor design, airfoil aerodynamics, scalable multi-objective benchmarks (DTLZ2 with P up to 100), multilayer optical thin-film design (P=128, L=64), and high-dimensional FashionMNIST image statistics (P=784 with a U-Net architecture).

The manuscript provides thorough robustness and ablation analyses, including verification under different parameter permutations, extensive ODE solver sweeps (Euler, RK4, adaptive Dormand-Prince), surrogate noise injection tests, and accuracy-conditioned diversity analyses.
The paper is exceptionally well-written, with clear exposition of the problem setup, intuitive figures, and transparent discussion of limitations.
weaknesses: The theoretical results (Propositions 4.1 and 4.2) are relatively elementary algebraic observations regarding coordinate permutations, serving more as formal validation of the design choice rather than deep theoretical breakthroughs.

The evaluation focuses exclusively on bidirectional invertible models (CFM and INN); comparisons against standard non-invertible conditional diffusion / conditional CFM baselines (where y is purely passed as a conditioning vector) are discussed conceptually but not benchmarked empirically for inverse synthesis accuracy and diversity.

On high-dimensional DTLZ benchmarks (P >= 50), coupling-based INNs achieve lower forward MSE than Diag–CFM, indicating that the zero-anchored bidirectional flow may face slight capacity trade-offs in pure forward surrogate regression at high dimensions.

strengths: Clear and well-motivated insight: The paper identifies a concrete pathology in adapting conditional flow matching (CFM) to bidirectional inverse problems—specifically, the arbitrary pairing of design coordinates with label coordinates, which introduces sensitivity to ordering and scale. The proposed zero-anchored Diagonal Flow Matching (Diag-CFM) neatly resolves this issue with provable permutation equivariance of the target velocity distribution.

Cost-free, architecture-intrinsic uncertainty quantification: The Zero-Deviation metric is a particularly elegant byproduct of the zero-anchoring formulation, measuring drift in the anchored label coordinates at $t=1$ with zero additional forward passes. Together with Self-Consistency, it consistently outperforms standard deep ensembles and flow-matching loss baselines across candidate selection, abstention, and out-of-distribution detection.

Comprehensive and rigorous experimental validation: The empirical evaluation spans diverse domains from low-dimensional engineering systems (gas turbine combustor, airfoil aerodynamics) to scalable multi-objective benchmarks (DTLZ2 up to $P=100$), optical thin-film coatings ($P=128$), and pixel-level image statistics ($P=784$).

Thorough diagnostic analyses: The paper provides insightful analyses that address potential confounders, including accuracy-conditioned diversity curves (avoiding misleading diversity scores from inaccurate models), sensitivity across ODE numerical integrators (Euler, RK4, Dopri5), and robustness to surrogate model approximations.
weaknesses: Comparison to unidirectional conditional generative models: The baselines focus on bidirectional models (coupling INNs and concatenated CFM). While bidirectional modeling offers simultaneous forward surrogate evaluation and self-consistency checking, comparing inverse design quality against standard unidirectional conditional flow matching or diffusion models (where target labels $y^*$ condition the vector field via FiLM/cross-attention from pure noise $z \in \mathbb{R}^P$) would clarify whether the bidirectional constraint imposes any trade-offs in sample quality.

Lack of formal calibration for abstention: The UQ metrics are evaluated using ranking/AUC and relative error reduction across fixed rejection percentiles, but the paper does not provide guidance or frameworks (such as conformal prediction) for selecting absolute abstention thresholds with statistical guarantees in practical deployments.

Relatively elementary theoretical contribution: Propositions 4.1 and 4.2 are straightforward linear algebraic observations regarding coordinate permutations. The value of the paper lies predominantly in its empirical realization and the resulting architectural uncertainty mechanics rather than deep theoretical results.

strengths: Simple, elegant, and theoretically grounded core idea: Diag–CFM addresses a genuine pathology in naive conditional flow matching for inverse design—namely, coordinate-pairing asymmetry and ordering sensitivity—by introducing a zero-anchoring scheme that provably renders the target velocity distribution equivariant under coordinate permutations.

Clever, zero-overhead uncertainty quantification: The zero-anchoring formulation enables the 'Zero-Deviation' metric, which quantifies epistemic uncertainty directly from the synthesis endpoint residual at t=1 with zero additional model evaluations or forward passes, consistently matching or beating 5-model deep ensembles across several evaluation tasks.

Comprehensive empirical evaluation: The paper evaluates across five diverse benchmark tasks ranging from low-dimensional engineering systems (gas turbine combustor P=6, airfoil P=14) to high-dimensional problems (thin film optical coating P=128, FashionMNIST image statistics P=784) and scalable multi-objective benchmarks (DTLZ2 up to P=100).

Thorough validation using exact analytical maps and robustness checks: Unlike many works that rely solely on learned forward surrogates, the authors use exact physics/analytical forward evaluations for DTLZ, thin-film coating (TMM), and FashionMNIST, and provide extensive robustness sweeps for surrogate noise, alternative surrogate architectures, coordinate orderings, and ODE numerical solvers (Euler, RK4, adaptive Dopri5).

Effective framing of generative diversity: The accuracy-conditioned diversity analysis convincingly demonstrates that raw diversity metrics in prior baselines were inflated by inaccurate candidate solutions, whereas Diag–CFM maintains true solution diversity at stringent tolerance thresholds.
weaknesses: Dimension expansion overhead when label dimension L is comparable to P: Augmenting the state from P to P+L is negligible when L << P, but becomes noticeable when L is large relative to P (e.g., in the thin film setting where P=128 and L=64, expanding the state space by 50%). The paper would benefit from discussing the computational and memory scaling limits of this state augmentation.

Absence of unidirectional conditional diffusion / flow matching baselines: The empirical comparison is strictly focused on bidirectional/invertible models (coupling-based INNs and standard CFM). While this directly isolates the effect of the invertible bidirectional formulation, benchmarking against standard unidirectional conditional diffusion/CFM models (e.g., conditioning via FiLM/cross-attention mapping noise directly to designs) would clarify whether invertibility incurs any generative fidelity penalty compared to unidirectional models.

Forward prediction degradation at higher dimensions in DTLZ: On DTLZ2 at P=50 and P=100, coupling INNs achieve lower forward MSE than Diag–CFM. While the authors transparently acknowledge this in the limitations section, deeper diagnostic analysis explaining why INN forward prediction retains an advantage in this specific regime would strengthen the paper.
